neighbours.label: the setting of sitting a timed exam: the word 'exam' / 'examination' together with its time limits and hall rules; the same rules for other events stay quiet
fire: Students may not use a dictionary during the exam, and phones must be switched off.
The final examination lasts three hours and is held in the sports hall.
Each candidate gets fifteen extra minutes to read the questions before the exam begins.
Nobody may leave the room in the first half hour of the written exam.
For the physics exam you are allowed one page of handwritten notes.
The invigilator collected the answer sheets as soon as the exam ended.
She ran out of time in the maths exam and left two questions blank.
Calculators are banned in the first paper of the entrance examination.
quiet: Guests may not use a camera during the concert, and phones must be switched off.
The annual meeting lasts three hours and is held in the sports hall.
Each runner gets fifteen extra minutes to warm up before the race begins.
Nobody may leave the theatre in the first half hour of the play.
For the long hike you are allowed one small bag of personal items.
The waiter collected the empty plates as soon as the dinner ended.
She ran out of flour in the kitchen and left two cakes unbaked.
Umbrellas are banned in the first row of the open-air cinema.

notes: Probes: 'during the exam' 0.92, 'In the written examination, candidates are allowed to bring' 0.52, 'The chemistry paper lasts 90 minutes' 0.25, polling stations and voting 0.21, 'state reading test' 0.18; the same rules in a library 0.01, a 90-minute train ride 0.04. The top examples also include polling/voting, so the pole may be wider than exams (a supervised, rule-bound sitting).
